Choose by Application

Start with the requirements of your material, formulation and process. Open detailed application guidance to frame the evaluation; listed grades are starting points, not rankings or suitability guarantees.

Coatings

Compare TiO₂ candidates in the coating formulation and prepared film you will actually use, with matched processing, exposure and endpoint methods.

Key evaluation factors
  • Binder, vehicle and pigment loading basis
  • Dispersion route and process history
  • Substrate, film construction and cure
  • Hiding, colour or undertone, and gloss as separate endpoints
  • Exposure, rheology and stated test methods

Plastics

Evaluate TiO₂ in the defined resin, incorporation route and converted specimen against the appearance, defect and exposure results you require.

Key evaluation factors
  • Resin system and TiO₂ incorporation route
  • Conversion process and specimen geometry
  • Whiteness, opacity and surface appearance
  • Dispersion screens and defect observations
  • Exposure requirements and stated test methods

Masterbatch

Evaluate TiO₂ as an input through concentrate processing and final-article performance. The product offered is TiO₂ input, not finished masterbatch.

Key evaluation factors
  • Carrier and receiving resin
  • Pigment loading in concentrate and final article
  • Concentrate preparation and processing
  • Let-down and conversion behavior
  • Final-article optical and performance endpoints

Printing Inks

Evaluate TiO₂ in the prepared ink and printed white layer, with the ink vehicle, print route and substrate defined.

Key evaluation factors
  • Ink vehicle and print process
  • Substrate, deposited layer and drying or cure
  • Opacity, coverage, colour and pinholes as distinct outcomes
  • Dispersion, rheology and storage behavior
  • Stated methods and print-system conditions
Explore Titanium Dioxide for Printing Inks

Grades to Review

  • M-350
  • M-510
  • M-52
  • M-2377

Paper

Evaluate TiO₂ in the intended furnish, addition route and finished-paper system under comparable production and measurement conditions.

Key evaluation factors
  • Furnish and addition route
  • Brightness
  • Whiteness and colour
  • Paper opacity
  • Dispersion, retention-related observations and method basis
Explore Titanium Dioxide for Paper

Grades to Review

  • M-350
  • M-2377

Specialty Materials

Review CR-901 against the composition, particle and process requirements of the intended specialty material. The grade’s typical data are evaluation inputs, not qualification results.

Grade-specific review points
  • TiO₂ and rutile content
  • Listed specific-surface-area options
  • Listed elemental impurity values versus buyer limits
  • Material composition and processing conditions
